tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

def search(self, query_embedding: List[float], limit: int = 5, source_filter: str = None, access_weight: float = 0.0) -> List[Dict]:
        if not query_embedding: return []
        
        q_emb_np = np.array(query_embedding, dtype='float32')
        candidate_ids = []
        candidate_scores = {}
        current_time = int(time.time())

        # Determine if we can use FAISS
        use_faiss = FAISS_AVAILABLE and self.faiss_index and self.faiss_index.ntotal > 0

        # 1. FAISS Search
        if use_faiss:
            with self.faiss_lock:
                q_emb_2d = q_emb_np.reshape(1, -1)
                faiss.normalize_L2(q_emb_2d)
                scores, indices = self.faiss_index.search(q_emb_2d, limit * 2)
                
                for i, idx in enumerate(indices[0]):
                    if idx != -1:
                        candidate_ids.append(int(idx))
                        candidate_scores[int(idx)] = float(scores[0][i])

        # 2. Linear Fallback (If FAISS is missing or empty)
        else:
            try:
                with self._connect() as con:
                    rows = con.execute("""
                        SELECT id, embedding FROM memories 
                        WHERE deleted = 0 AND parent_id IS NULL AND embedding IS NOT NULL
                        AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?)
                    """, (current_time,)).fetchall()
                
                # Normalize query
                q_norm = np.linalg.norm(q_emb_np)
                if q_norm > 0:
                    q_emb_np = q_emb_np / q_norm

                for r in rows:
                    emb = self._parse_embedding(r[1])
                    if emb is not None:
                        # Normalize target
                        e_norm = np.linalg.norm(emb)
                        if e_norm > 0:
                            emb = emb / e_norm
                        
                        score = np.dot(q_emb_np, emb)
                        candidate_ids.append(r[0])
                        candidate_scores[r[0]] = float(score)
            except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning(f"Linear search failed: {e}")

        # 3. Fetch Details
        results = []
        if candidate_ids:
            # Sort by score descending and take top K to minimize DB fetch
            candidate_ids.sort(key=lambda x: candidate_scores.get(x, 0), reverse=True)
            top_ids = candidate_ids[:limit]
            
            placeholders = ','.join(['?'] * len(top_ids))
            query = f"SELECT id, text, created_at, type, access_count FROM memories WHERE id IN ({placeholders}) AND deleted = 0 AND parent_id IS NULL"
            params = list(top_ids)
            
            if source_filter:
                query += " AND source = ?"
                params.append(source_filter)
            
            with self._connect() as con:
                rows = con.execute(query, params).fetchall()
                
                valid_ids = []
                for r in rows:
                    mid = r[0]
                    mem_expires_at = r[2]
                    access_count = r[4] if len(r) > 4 else 0
                    importance_boost = 0
                    
                    # Get expires_at for this memory
                    expires_at = con.execute("SELECT expires_at FROM memories WHERE id = ?", (mid,)).fetchone()
                    if expires_at and expires_at[0] and expires_at[0] < current_time:
                        continue  # Skip expired memories
                    
                    if mid in candidate_scores:
                        base_score = candidate_scores[mid]
                        boosted_score = base_score * (1 + access_count * access_weight) * (1 + importance_boost * 0.5)
                        results.append({
                            "id": mid,
                            "text": r[1],
                            "created_at": r[2],
                            "type": r[3],
                            "score": boosted_score
                        })
                        valid_ids.append(mid)
                
                # Increment access_count for returned memories
                if valid_ids:
                    placeholders = ','.join(['?'] * len(valid_ids))
                    con.execute(f"UPDATE memories SET access_count = access_count + 1 WHERE id IN ({placeholders})", valid_ids)
            
            results.sort(key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
            return results
        
        return []

Mark the module `enabled: false`, fix the import and node base class, implement perception recording, flow adoption, atomic state persistence, memory serialization and chat buffering, and cover the core lifecycle with `tests/test_autonomous_agent.py`. """Tests for the experimental autonomous agent runtime."""

import json

import pytest

from core.flow_evolution import FlowEvolutionError
from core.flow_manager import FlowManager, flow_manager as shared_flow_manager
from modules.autonomous_agent.core.communicator import AgentCommunicator
from modules.autonomous_agent.core.sandbox import FlowValidationError, SandboxViolation
from modules.autonomous_agent.core.service import AgentService
from modules.autonomous_agent.core.types import (
    AgentAction,
    ActionType,
    AgentConfig,
    Experience,
    FlowSpec,
    Perception,
)
from modules.autonomous_agent.nodes import NODE_EXECUTORS


class FakeProposer:
    def __init__(self, operations):
        self.operations = operations
        self.goals = []

    async def propose(self, flow, goal):
        self.goals.append(goal)
        return list(self.operations)


def make_agent(tmp_path, **overrides) -> AgentService:
    """Build an agent whose runtime files live under ``tmp_path``."""
    config = AgentConfig(
        agent_id=overrides.pop("agent_id", "test-agent"),
        persistence={
            "enabled": True,
            "state_path": str(tmp_path / "state.json"),
        },
        **overrides,
    )
    manager = FlowManager(storage_file=str(tmp_path / "ai_flows.json"))
    agent = AgentService(config, flow_manager=manager)
    agent.flows_store_path = tmp_path / "ai_flows.json"
    return agent


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_handle_user_message_records_perception_and_chat_ack(tmp_path):
    agent = make_agent(tmp_path)
    assert await agent.initialize() is True

    perception = await agent.handle_user_message("chat", "hello", "user-1")

    assert perception.content == "hello"
    assert perception.metadata["user_id"] == "user-1"
    assert agent.state.recent_perceptions[-1]["content"] == "hello"
    messages = agent.communicator.get_pending_chat_messages()
    assert messages
    assert messages[-1]["content"] == "Received. Processing..."

    ]

    return rows


def test_linear_search_fills_the_page_after_filtering(tmp_path):

def temp_modules_dir(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Creates a temporary module directory structure for testing."""
    modules_root = tmp_path
    modules_dir = modules_root / "modules"
    modules_dir.mkdir()
    (modules_dir / "__init__.py").touch()

    # Valid enabled module with a router
    (modules_dir / "enabled_module").mkdir()
    with open(modules_dir / "enabled_module" / "module.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"name": "Enabled Module", "enabled": True, "id": "enabled_module"}, f)
    (modules_dir / "enabled_module" / "__init__.py").write_text("from fastapi import APIRouter\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=['enabled_module'])\n@router.get('/')\ndef read_root(): return {}")

    # Valid disabled module
    (modules_dir / "disabled_module").mkdir()
    with open(modules_dir / "disabled_module" / "module.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"name": "Disabled Module", "enabled": False, "id": "disabled_module"}, f)
    (modules_dir / "disabled_module" / "__init__.py").write_text("from fastapi import APIRouter\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=['disabled_module'])\n@router.get('/')\ndef read_root(): return {}")

    # Unload the real 'modules' package if it was cached by other tests.
    # This prevents import conflicts and ensures our temporary modules are found.
    import importlib
    # Use monkeypatch to safely unload any previously imported 'modules' package.
    # This will be automatically undone after the test.
    for m in [mod for mod in sys.modules if mod.startswith('modules')]:
        monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, m, raising=False)

    # Add the temp dir to sys.path so importlib can find the modules
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(modules_root))
    
    # Invalidate import caches to ensure the new path is used
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    yield str(modules_dir)

class SafeHttpxClient:
    """
    Restricted HTTP client that enforces network security policies.
    """
    
    # Default allowed domains (can be configured)
    DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS: Set[str] = {
        'api.openai.com',
        'api.anthropic.com',
        'api.together.xyz',
        'api.groq.com',
        'api.cohere.com',
        'api.ai21.com',
        'api.perplexity.ai',
        'api.mistral.ai',
        'generativelanguage.googleapis.com',
        'api.replicate.com',
        'api.huggingface.co',
        'api.wolframalpha.com',
        'api.weatherapi.com',  # Weather tool
        'wttr.in',  # Weather tool (wttr.in JSON API)
        'api.frankfurter.app',  # Currency converter
        'en.wikipedia.org',  # Wikipedia
        'export.arxiv.org',  # ArXiv
        'www.youtube.com', 'youtube.com',  # YouTube transcripts
        'api.telegram.org',  # Telegram
        '127.0.0.1',  # Internal API for modules (BrowserAutomation)
        'localhost',  # Internal API for modules
        'github.com', 'www.github.com', 'raw.githubusercontent.com', # Added for FetchURL
    }
    
    # Allowed URL schemes
    ALLOWED_SCHEMES: Set[str] = {'http', 'https'}
    
    # Blocked IP ranges (IPv4)
    BLOCKED_IPV4_RANGES: List[str] = [
        # Note: 127.0.0.0/8 is implicitly permitted for authorized internal domains (like 127.0.0.1) 
        # but blocked for general arbitrary fetching unless domain matches.
        '10.0.0.0/8',       # Private Class A
        '172.16.0.0/12',    # Private Class B
        '192.168.0.0/16',   # Private Class C
        '169.254.0.0/16',   # Link-local
        '0.0.0.0/8',        # Current network
    ]
    
    # Blocked IP ranges (IPv6)
    BLOCKED_IPV6_RANGES: List[str] = [
        '::1/128',          # Loopback
        'fc00::/7',         # Unique local address (private)
        'fe80::/10',        # Link-local
        '::/128',           # Unspecified
        '::ffff:0:0/96',    # IPv4-mapped
    ]
    
    def __init__(self, allowed_domains: Optional[Set[str]] = None, 
                 timeout: float = 30.0,
                 max_response_size: int = 10 * 1024 * 1024,  # 10MB
                 max_redirects: int = 5):
        # None means "use the default allowlist"; an explicit empty set means no network.
        self.allowed_domains = (
            set(self.DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DOMAINS)
            if allowed_domains is None else set(allowed_domains)
        )
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.max_response_size = max_response_size
        self.max_redirects = max(0, int(max_redirects))
        
        # Import ipaddress for proper CIDR-based IP validation
        import ipaddress
        self._ipaddress = ipaddress
        
        # Pre-compile IPv4 blocking patterns
        self._blocked_ipv4_networks = []
        for cidr in self.BLOCKED_IPV4_RANGES:
            try:
                self._blocked_ipv4_networks.append(ipaddress.ip_network(cidr, strict=False))
            except ValueError as _exc:
                logger.debug("ignored exception: %s", _exc)
        
        # Pre-compile IPv6 blocking patterns  
        self._blocked_ipv6_networks = []
        for cidr in self.BLOCKED_IPV6_RANGES:
            try:
                self._blocked_ipv6_networks.append(ipaddress.ip_network(cidr, strict=False))
            except ValueError as _exc:
                logger.debug("ignored exception: %s", _exc)
    
    def _is_domain_allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        """Check if a URL's domain is in the allowed list."""
        from urllib.parse import urlparse

        if not self.allowed_domains:
            return False
        
        try:
            parsed = urlparse(url)
            domain = parsed.netloc.lower()
            
            # Remove port if present
            if ':' in domain:
                domain = domain.split(':')[0]
            
            # Check exact match or subdomain match
            for allowed in self.allowed_domains:
                if domain == allowed or domain.endswith('.' + allowed):
                    return True
            
            return False
        except Exception:
            return False
    
    def _is_ip_blocked(self, host: str) -> bool:
        """Check if a host/IP is in blocked ranges using CIDR notation."""
        try:
            # Try to parse as IP address directly
            ip = self._ipaddress.ip_address(host)
            
            # Check IPv4 blocked ranges
            if isinstance(ip, self._ipaddress.IPv4Address):
                for network in self._blocked_ipv4_networks:
                    if ip in network:
                        return True
            
            # Check IPv6 blocked ranges
            if isinstance(ip, self._ipaddress.IPv6Address):
                for network in self._blocked_ipv6_networks:
                    if ip in network:
                        return True
            
            return False
        except ValueError:
            # Not an IP address, allow through (domain check happens elsewhere)
            return False
    
    def _resolve_and_validate_ip(self, hostname: str) -> str:
        """
        Resolve hostname and validate every resulting IP.
        
        Uses getaddrinfo for IPv4/IPv6 support instead of gethostbyname.
        
        Returns:
            The first resolved IP address (all answers were validated)
            
        Raises:
            SecurityError: If any answer is blocked or resolution fails. A host that returns
                both public and private addresses is rejected as a whole: accepting the public
                answer would leave the client free to connect to the private one.
        """
        import socket
        
        try:
            # getaddrinfo returns list of (family, type, proto, canonname, sockaddr)
            # We want to check both IPv4 and IPv6 results
            results = socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None, socket.AF_UNSPEC, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            
            if not results:
                raise SecurityError(f"Could not resolve domain '{hostname}' - no DNS results")
            
            resolved_ips = [sockaddr[0] for _, _, _, _, sockaddr in results]
            blocked = [ip_addr for ip_addr in resolved_ips if self._is_ip_blocked(ip_addr)]
            if blocked:
                raise SecurityError(
                    f"Domain '{hostname}' resolves to blocked IP addresses: {blocked}"
                )
            return resolved_ips[0]
            
        except socket.gaierror:
            raise SecurityError(f"Could not resolve domain '{hostname}' - DNS lookup failed")
        except socket.herror:
            raise SecurityError(f"Could not resolve domain '{hostname}' - host not found")
    
    def _validate_target(self, url: str) -> None:
        """Validate scheme, allowlist and every DNS answer for one request target."""
        from urllib.parse import urlparse

        parsed = urlparse(url)
        if parsed.scheme.lower() not in self.ALLOWED_SCHEMES:
            raise SecurityError(
                f"URL scheme '{parsed.scheme}' is not allowed. "
                f"Only {', '.join(self.ALLOWED_SCHEMES)} are permitted."
            )
        hostname = parsed.hostname
        if not hostname:
            raise SecurityError(f"Invalid URL '{url}': no hostname found")
        hostname = hostname.lower()
        if not self._is_domain_allowed(url):
            raise SecurityError(
                f"HTTP requests to '{url}' are not permitted. Domain not in whitelist."
            )
        self._resolve_and_validate_ip(hostname)

    def request(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs):
        """Make a restricted HTTP request.

        Redirects are followed manually so every destination is re-validated against the
        scheme, hostname and DNS policy. The body is streamed into a bounded buffer instead of
        being buffered by httpx first, so an oversized response cannot exhaust memory.

        Note: DNS is validated immediately before the request, but Python's HTTP stack resolves
        the name again while connecting. Pinning the validated address to that connection needs
        transport-level support; until then this is defense in depth, not a complete SSRF
        boundary.
        """
        import httpx
        from urllib.parse import urljoin

        kwargs = dict(kwargs)
        kwargs.pop("follow_redirects", None)
        supplied_timeout = kwargs.get("timeout", self.timeout)
        try:
            timeout = min(float(supplied_timeout), float(self.timeout))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            timeout = self.timeout
        kwargs["timeout"] = timeout

        current_url = url
        current_method = str(method).upper()
        current_kwargs = kwargs
        with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=False, timeout=timeout, trust_env=False) as client:
            for hop in range(self.max_redirects + 1):
                self._validate_target(current_url)
                request = client.build_request(current_method, current_url, **current_kwargs)
                response = client.send(request, stream=True)
                try:
                    if response.is_redirect:
                        location = response.headers.get("location")
                        if not location:
                            raise SecurityError(f"Redirect from '{current_url}' has no location")
                        if hop >= self.max_redirects:
                            raise SecurityError(
                                f"Too many redirects while requesting '{url}'"
                            )
                        current_url = urljoin(str(response.url), location)
                        if response.status_code in (301, 302, 303) \
                                and current_method not in ("GET", "HEAD"):
                            current_method = "GET"
                            current_kwargs = {
                                key: value for key, value in current_kwargs.items()
                                if key not in ("json", "data", "content", "files")
                            }
                        continue

                    chunks = []
                    total = 0
                    for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
                        total += len(chunk)
                        if total > self.max_response_size:
                            raise ResourceLimitError(
                                f"Response size exceeds maximum allowed "
                                f"({self.max_response_size} bytes)"
                            )
                        chunks.append(chunk)
                    headers = [
                        (key, value) for key, value in response.headers.multi_items()
                        if key.lower() not in (
                            "content-encoding", "content-length", "transfer-encoding",
                        )
                    ]
                    return httpx.Response(
                        response.status_code,
                        headers=headers,
                        content=b"".join(chunks),
                        request=response.request,
                    )
                finally:
                    response.close()
        raise SecurityError(f"Too many redirects while requesting '{url}'")
    
    def get(self, url: str, **kwargs):
        return self.request('GET', url, **kwargs)
    
    def post(self, url: str, **kwargs):

+description: "DAG execution patterns, bridge groups, conditional routing, and loop guards for NeuroCore flows"
+All NeuroCore workflows are **Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)** executed by `core/flow_runner.py`. Understanding these patterns is essential for designing effective flows.
+2. Start with nodes having in-degree 0 (entry points)
+3. Process nodes, decrementing in-degree of downstream nodes

+- Nodes within a bridge group execute concurrently
+- Bridge groups execute sequentially (group N waits for group N-1)

+# In a conditional node's receive() method

FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Runtime dependencies only (test tools live in requirements-dev.txt). The compiler is needed
# only while wheels build, so it is installed and purged in the same layer.
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc \
    && pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt \
    && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove gcc \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Run as an unprivileged user. UID 1000 matches the usual first Linux user, so the bind-mounted
# ./data and ./modules stay writable; docker-compose.yml can override it per host.
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 neurocore

COPY --chown=neurocore:neurocore . .
RUN mkdir -p data && chown neurocore:neurocore data

USER neurocore

EXPOSE 8000

# Bind all interfaces inside the container so a published port works. Remote exposure is
# bounded by the host publish mapping (loopback-only in docker-compose.yml). A bare
# `docker run` without NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN refuses to start rather than run unauthenticated.
ENV NEUROCORE_HOST=0.0.0.0

CMD ["python", "main.py"]

    strategy:

Or with Docker:

Docker keeps all mutable state in `./data` (`NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR=/app/data`) and

playwright install chromium

## 🔒 Security Defaults

NeuroCore is a control plane with no authentication, so it stays local by default. Remote
access, the auto-reloader and secret-bearing exports are each an explicit opt-in:

| Environment variable | Default | Effect when set |
|---|---|---|
| `NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR` | project root | Store settings, flows, chats, calendar events and databases in one directory (Docker uses `/app/data`) |
| `NEUROCORE_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind another interface (Docker uses `0.0.0.0` inside the container) |
| `NEUROCORE_PORT` | `8000` | Bind another port |
| `NEUROCORE_RELOAD` | off | Enable uvicorn auto-reload |
| `NEUROCORE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | loopback only | Accept extra `Host` names |
| `NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN` | unset | Require a token from non-loopback clients |
| `NEUROCORE_BRAIN_TOKEN` | unset | Required for all remote `/brain/*` access; send `X-Brain-Token`, optional `X-Brain-Actor` |
| `NEUROCORE_EXPORT_SECRETS` | off | Include secrets in the config export |

State-changing requests are rejected when their `Origin` is cross-origin (CSRF). Marketplace
packages are extracted through a path-confined helper, tool code runs in a sandbox whose
first-party imports are allowlisted, and secrets are stripped from config exports and masked in
debug logs.

700:### ADR-034: Brain ledgers reload and mutate under one cross-process lock
- **Date**: 2026-10-24
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Each brain store kept its ledger in process memory and rewrote the whole file through
  a temp-file replace. Two workers or two server processes could each load the same ledger, apply a
  change and overwrite the other's update, losing outcomes, candidates, configuration changes,
  kernel blocks, reactions or actors.
- **Decision**:
  1. Add `modules/brain/persistence.py` with `LedgerLock` (a thread re-entrant guard plus a
     `filelock.FileLock` on `<ledger>.lock`), `atomic_write_json` (fsynced temp file plus
     `os.replace`) and the `engine_transaction`, `engine_transaction_async` and
     `ledger_transaction` decorators.
  2. Every brain store owns a `LedgerLock` and its `load`/`save` run while it is held. Mutating
     engine methods are decorated, so they reload the ledger, apply one change and persist it
     before another writer can interleave. Nested engine calls reuse the outer transaction.
  3. The learning, improvement, configuration, kernel, reactivity and actor ledgers are
     covered. Evaluation last/baseline, drift baseline and brain state files use the same lock
     and atomic write without reloading, because their writes are whole-snapshot replacements.
  4. A lock wait is bounded at 10 seconds and then fails with `filelock.Timeout`; the lock is
     never held across a provider or LLM call.
- **Consequences**:
  - *Positive*: Concurrent workers keep each other's ledger changes; the nine copied temp-file
    write blocks become one tested helper.
  - *Trade-offs*: A `.lock` file sits beside every brain ledger; the brain state file remains
    last-writer-wins because it describes the local runtime, not durable knowledge; a stuck
    holder delays a writer for up to 10 seconds.

### ADR-035: Audit P0 hardening fails closed and states its limits
- **Date**: 2026-10-25
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: An external audit of `e491655` reported: no token check for remote clients when
  `NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN` was unset; an in-process fallback when the tool worker could not start;
  tools reading the whole process environment; a network policy that accepted mixed DNS answers,
  skipped redirect targets, buffered whole responses and treated an empty allowlist as "default";
  a hostname-only CSRF check; an unused worker pool that could not run; an agent flow pattern
  that raised `KeyError`; memory search returning short pages; and diverging dependency files.
  Verification confirmed these, rejected one claim (the agent's `llm_module` node type is the
  type the LLM dispatcher handles; `llm_core` does not exist) and found more: two agent templates
  (`telegram_output`, `kb_query`) no module dispatches, credentials forwarded on cross-host
  redirects, untested S2/S3/S4 fixes, and `module.json` files truncated to 0 bytes because
  manifests were rewritten in place while concurrent test runs read them.
- **Decision**:
  1. A non-loopback bind refuses to start without a token unless
     `NEUROCORE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_REMOTE=1`; the middleware rejects tokenless non-loopback
     clients on the same terms. Origins compare scheme, host and effective port.
  2. A tool worker that cannot start raises `SandboxStartupError`; tool code never runs in the
     application process. Tools see only the `env_allowlist` values. The HTTP client rejects any
     blocked DNS answer, re-validates every redirect, drops `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`,
     `Cookie`, `auth` and `cookies` when a redirect changes origin, streams under a byte cap and
     treats `allowed_domains=set()` as no network. README calls this defense in depth, not OS
     isolation.
  3. `modules/tools/sandbox_manager.py` is deleted: nothing imported it and it used
     `queue.Queue` as inter-process transport.
  4. Agent templates dispatch to `messaging_output` (platform pinned to `telegram`) and
     `query_knowledge`; a `scheduled_task` pattern replaces the missing `repeater_node` pattern.
     Tests resolve every template through `FlowRunner._get_executor_class`.
  5. Semantic memory search filters source, parent, deletion and expiry in SQL, walking ranked
     candidates in batches until the page fills; FAISS ranks every vector.
  6. `ModuleManager` writes `module.json` through `_write_manifest` (serialize, fsynced temp file,
     `os.replace`).
  7. `pyproject.toml` is the dependency source of truth: `scipy` becomes core (built-in statistics
     routes import it), `requirements.txt` is runtime plus the browser/documents/messaging extras,
     `requirements-dev.txt` adds the `dev` extra, and `tests/test_packaging.py` enforces it. The
     Docker image installs runtime requirements only, purges `gcc` and runs as UID 1000; compose
     maps `NEUROCORE_UID`/`NEUROCORE_GID` and sets the unauthenticated-remote opt-out its loopback
     publish justifies. `data/.gitkeep` is tracked so the bind mount keeps host ownership. CI runs
     Linux 3.12/3.13, Windows 3.12 and a Docker build that must refuse a tokenless start.
  8. Test change: `test_os_getenv_works` asserted that tools read the inherited environment, the
     behaviour item 2 removes. It is replaced by `test_os_getenv_hides_the_inherited_environment`
     and `test_os_getenv_reads_permitted_values`.
- **Consequences**:
  - *Positive*: Misconfiguration fails at startup instead of exposing the control plane; sandbox
    isolation never degrades silently; secrets reach a tool only by name; every security fix has
    a regression test; agent flows dispatch; manifests cannot be left truncated.
  - *Trade-offs*: Deployments that bound `0.0.0.0` without a token must now set one or the
    opt-out; tools that read arbitrary environment variables must list them in `env_allowlist`;
    `pip install -r requirements.txt` no longer installs pytest; a Linux host user other than
    UID 1000 must set `NEUROCORE_UID`; DNS is still resolved again at connect time, so pinning the
    validated address remains open, as do cycle rejection by default (F1) and a container
    boundary for untrusted tools (S6).
'''
open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="").write((s.rstrip("\r\n").replace("\r\n","\n")+adr).replace("\n",nl))
EOF
tail -3 .aikit/decisions.md

  redirects, untested S2/S3/S4 fixes, and `module.json` files truncated to 0 bytes because
  manifests were rewritten in place while concurrent test runs read them.

     `NEUROCORE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_REMOTE=1`; the middleware rejects tokenless non-loopback

     application process. Tools see only the `env_allowlist` values. The HTTP client rejects any

     treats `allowed_domains=set()` as no network. README calls this defense in depth, not OS
     isolation.

     `queue.Queue` as inter-process transport.

     `query_knowledge`; a `scheduled_task` pattern replaces the missing `repeater_node` pattern.

  5. Semantic memory search filters source, parent, deletion and expiry in SQL, walking ranked
     candidates in batches until the page fills; FAISS ranks every vector.
  6. `ModuleManager` writes `module.json` through `_write_manifest` (serialize, fsynced temp file,
     `os.replace`).
  7. `pyproject.toml` is the dependency source of truth: `scipy` becomes core (built-in statistics
     routes import it), `requirements.txt` is runtime plus the browser/documents/messaging extras,
     `requirements-dev.txt` adds the `dev` extra, and `tests/test_packaging.py` enforces it. The

1	"""Absolute locations for NeuroCore runtime files.
2	
3	Runtime state must never depend on the process working directory: starting the app or
4	its tests from a parent folder must not create settings, databases or caches there.
5	"""
6	
7	import os
8	from pathlib import Path
9	
10	PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
11	
12	
13	def project_path(*parts: str) -> str:
14	    """Return an absolute path inside the NeuroCore project root."""
15	    return str(PROJECT_ROOT.joinpath(*parts))
16	
17	
18	def state_path(*parts: str) -> str:
19	    """Return a path for mutable state, honouring NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR.
20	
21	    Docker deployments mount one data directory and set NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR, so
22	    root-level state files do not silently disappear when a container is recreated.
23	    """
24	    root = os.environ.get("NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR") or PROJECT_ROOT

"""Absolute locations for NeuroCore runtime files.

Runtime state must never depend on the process working directory: starting the app or
its tests from a parent folder must not create settings, databases or caches there.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def project_path(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Return an absolute path inside the NeuroCore project root."""
    return str(PROJECT_ROOT.joinpath(*parts))


def state_path(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Return a path for mutable state, honouring NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR.

    Docker deployments mount one data directory and set NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR, so
    root-level state files do not silently disappear when a container is recreated.
    """
    root = os.environ.get("NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR") or PROJECT_ROOT
    return str(Path(root).expanduser().resolve().joinpath(*parts))

"""
Pytest configuration and fixtures for test isolation.

Provides fixtures to backup/restore files that are mutated in-place during tests,
ensuring test isolation and preventing cross-test contamination.
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

import pytest

# Tests use project-relative paths throughout. Anchor collection to the project folder so
# running pytest from a parent directory cannot create state files beside the parent.
PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
os.chdir(PROJECT_ROOT)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preserve the real faiss module reference BEFORE any test file is collected.
#
# test_memory_backend.py installs a MagicMock as sys.modules['faiss'] at
# module level (collection time) so that MemoryStore tests don't need a real
# FAISS installation.  Unfortunately this also poisons sys.modules for every
# other test that imports faiss later — in particular the
# TestFaissDimensionMismatchWarning tests in test_knowledge_base.py.
#
# By capturing the real module here (conftest.py is imported before any test
# file) we can restore it for tests that expect real FAISS.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
try:
    import faiss as _real_faiss_module
except ImportError:
    _real_faiss_module = None


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def reset_shared_async_state():
    """
    Reset module-level async singletons between tests.

    httpx.AsyncClient and asyncio.Lock are bound to the event loop that
    created them.  With asyncio_mode='auto', each test gets its own loop,
    so a client created in test N is invalid in test N+1.  Resetting the
    globals before (and after) each test forces lazy re-creation in the
    correct loop without touching the old loop's handles.

    We intentionally do NOT call client.aclose() here — doing so via
    loop.run_until_complete() during test teardown invalidates Win32 pipe
    handles that multiprocessing tests created later rely on.  The client
    reference is simply dropped; httpx will issue a ResourceWarning on GC
    but that is harmless in test runs.
    """

"""Runtime state must stay inside the project, whatever the launch directory is."""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from core.flow_manager import FLOWS_FILE
from core.module_manager import MODULES_DIR
from core.observability import get_trace_file_path
from core.paths import PROJECT_ROOT
from core.session_manager import EPISODE_DIR, SESSION_FILE, TRACE_FILE
from core.settings import SETTINGS_FILE
from modules.calendar.events import EVENTS_FILE
from modules.chat.sessions import SESSIONS_FILE
from modules.reasoning_book.service import DATA_FILE

RUNTIME_PATHS = (
    SETTINGS_FILE,
    FLOWS_FILE,
    MODULES_DIR,
    SESSION_FILE,
    TRACE_FILE,
    EPISODE_DIR,
    get_trace_file_path(),
    EVENTS_FILE,
    SESSIONS_FILE,
    DATA_FILE,
)


def test_runtime_paths_are_absolute_and_inside_project():
    for runtime_path in RUNTIME_PATHS:
        path = Path(runtime_path)
        assert path.is_absolute(), runtime_path
        assert path == PROJECT_ROOT or PROJECT_ROOT in path.parents, runtime_path


def test_importing_the_app_from_another_directory_writes_nothing_there(tmp_path):
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(PROJECT_ROOT) + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", "import main"],
        cwd=tmp_path,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=120,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr

content.text:
I went through the audit finding by finding, and the planned fixes are done: all four project gates pass, including the full test suite. Nothing is committed. Another agent (`kilo:neurocore`) had already started this exact task and stopped about a day ago, so I took over its task record and finished its plan.

**Something you need to know first.** While I was testing, the root `ai_flows.json` was emptied, along with five `module.json` files. The cause was a test helper that saved a copy of those files before every test and wrote it back afterwards. When two test runs overlapped, one captured a half-written empty file and then kept writing that empty copy back after every later test. I set off the first overlap by running a full suite in the background while running smaller test batches. I restored the five `module.json` files from git. `ai_flows.json` isn't tracked by git and had no backup, so whatever it held is gone. Your `settings.json` in that folder only has default values (no API key, no active flows), so it probably only held default or test flows, but I can't confirm that. I deleted the empty copies so NeuroCore recreates its default flow on the next start.

I fixed the cause:
- Each test run now gets its own temporary folder for settings, flows and chats.
- The backup is taken once per run and checked before tests start.
- Files are restored without ever being left half-written.

To check it, I ran two full test suites at the same time. Afterwards every `module.json`, `settings.json` and `calendar_events.json` was unchanged. Tests still write two files in the real `data/` folder: `data/memory.sqlite3` and `data/reasoning_book.json`.

**Audit findings that were correct and are now fixed**

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| S1 remote login check skipped when no token is set; S5 cross-site request check ignores port and scheme | Already fixed by the earlier agent, with tests |
| S2 tool code falls back to running inside the app; S3 tools can read all environment variables; S4 network rules (mixed DNS answers, redirects, response size, empty allowlist) | Already fixed but **had no tests**. I added them. |
| W1/W2 broken worker pool | Confirmed. Nothing used it, so I deleted `modules/tools/sandbox_manager.py`. |
| A1-A scheduled request crashes with `KeyError` | Added the missing `scheduled_task` pattern |
| M1 memory search returns fewer results than asked | Filters now run before results are cut to the limit, in one query |
| O1 dependency files disagree; O2 Docker image includes test tools and runs as root | `pyproject.toml` is now the single source, and a new test keeps the requirements files in line with it. The image now has runtime packages only and runs as a normal user. CI runs on Linux and Windows, plus a Docker build check. |

**Where the audit was wrong or missed things**
- **A1-C is wrong:** the LLM module really does use `llm_module`; `llm_core` doesn't exist.
- **Two agent flow nodes could never run:** `telegram_output` and `kb_query` match no module. They now map to `messaging_output` (set to Telegram) and `query_knowledge`. A new test checks every template against the real dispatcher.
- **Logins leaked through redirects:** the tool's web client sent `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers on to a different host after a redirect. Fixed, with a test.
- **The earlier login fix broke Docker:** `docker-compose.yml` would no longer start. I set the explicit opt-out there, which is safe only because the port is published on `127.0.0.1` only.
- **Docs out of date:** `docs/TOOL_GUIDE.md` said tools can read any environment variable, and the README called the sandbox fully isolating. Both are corrected.

**Changes you might notice**
- `pip install -r requirements.txt` no longer installs pytest; tests now need `requirements-dev.txt`.
- Tools that read environment variables must list them in `env_allowlist` in `modules/tools/module.json`.
- On Linux, if your user ID isn't 1000, start Docker with `NEUROCORE_UID` and `NEUROCORE_GID` set.
- I replaced `test_os_getenv_works`, which expected the old, unsafe behaviour, with two tests for the new rule. This is recorded in decision record ADR-035.

**Not checked or still open**
- The Docker image build is **untested** locally because Docker Desktop wasn't running. The new CI job covers it.
- Not addressed: F1 (loops in a flow are still allowed by default, which changes behaviour and is your call), S6 (a container boundary for untrusted tools), DNS address pinning, the two `data/` files above, and the three leftover `tmp*.tmp` files from earlier sessions in the project root.

Do you want me to commit this as milestone commits, and should loops in flows be rejected by default (F1)?

    async def _get_executor_class(cls, module_id: str, node_type_id: str):
        """Thread-safe method to get or create an executor class from the cache."""
        cache_key = f"{module_id}.{node_type_id}"
        
        async with cls._get_cache_lock():
            # Check if already in cache (after acquiring lock)
            if cache_key in cls._executor_cache:
                return cls._executor_cache[cache_key]
            
            # Manage cache size before adding new entry
            cls._manage_cache_size()
            
            # Dynamically import the module's node logic dispatcher
            node_dispatcher = importlib.import_module(f"modules.{module_id}.node")
            # Only reload in debug mode to pick up hot-code changes;
            # in production this is wasteful and can cause state issues.
            if settings.get("debug_mode") and isinstance(node_dispatcher, types.ModuleType) and node_dispatcher.__name__ in sys.modules:
                # Invalidate cache before reloading to ensure fresh class is used
                cls._executor_cache.pop(cache_key, None)
                importlib.reload(node_dispatcher)
            # Get the specific executor class for this node type.
            # get_executor_class must be async; guard against sync variants to
            # produce a clear error instead of the cryptic "object type can't
            # be used in 'await' expression" TypeError.
            get_fn = node_dispatcher.get_executor_class
            if not asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(get_fn):

                )
            executor_class = await get_fn(node_type_id)
            cls._executor_cache[cache_key] = executor_class

def test_concurrent_write_is_seen_even_with_a_coarse_file_clock(tmp_path):
    import os

    store = str(tmp_path / "sessions.json")
    first = SessionManager(storage_file=store)
    first.create_session("from first")
    stamp = os.stat(store).st_mtime_ns
    second = SessionManager(storage_file=store)
    second.create_session("from second")
    # A 1-2 second filesystem clock can give the second write the first write's timestamp.
    os.utime(store, ns=(stamp, stamp))

    first.create_session("first again")

    names = {s["name"] for s in SessionManager(storage_file=store).sessions.values()}
    assert names == {"from first", "from second", "first again"}
EOF

async def initialize(self) -> bool:
        """Initialize the agent and all components."""
        try:
            # Attach the shared flow store so edits persist and gain version history.
            self.flow_creator.flow_manager = self.flow_manager
            self.evolution = FlowEvolution(
                self.flow_manager,
                allowed_node_types=node_template_types(),
                allowed_tools=set(
                    (self.config.sandbox or {}).get("allowed_tools", [])
                ),
            )

            # Load existing flows from NeuroCore
            await self._load_existing_flows()
            
            # Load memory from persistence
            await self._load_memory()
            
            # Initialize self-model
            # (SelfModel initializes automatically)
            
            self.state.initialized = True
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.state.errors.append({
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "phase": "initialization",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return False
    
    async def start(self) -> None:
        """Start the agent's cognitive loop."""
        if self.state.running:
            return
        
        if not self.state.initialized:
            await self.initialize()
        
        self.state.running = True
        
        # Start background tasks
        self._cognitive_task = asyncio.create_task(self._cognitive_loop())
        self._queue_task = asyncio.create_task(self._queue_processor())
        self._consolidation_task = asyncio.create_task(self._periodic_consolidation())
    
    async def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the agent gracefully."""
        self.state.running = False

        """Execute the requested flow, falling back to the active chat flow."""
        requested = action.parameters.get("flow_id")

            active = settings.get("active_ai_flows", []) or []
            if (not self.sandbox.check_flow_ownership(requested)

        return {"flow_id": flow_id, "status": "completed", "result": result}

        """Execute memory storage."""
        content = action.parameters.get("content", "")

content.content:
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Approval endpoints accepted `approved_by` from the request body, so any caller could
  choose the audit name. Remote access also had no brain-specific credential.
- **Decision**:
  1. All `/brain/*` routes share a `get_brain_actor` dependency. Loopback/test clients are trusted
     as `local` (or an optional `X-Brain-Actor` label); non-local clients must present
     `NEUROCORE_BRAIN_TOKEN` via `X-Brain-Token` (constant-time compare) and receive `401` on a
     missing/wrong token.
  2. Mutating routes use the authenticated actor name for promotion, configuration, kernel and
     drift-baseline audit records; the body `approved_by` field is ignored.
  3. `GET /brain/actor` reports the resolved name, role and whether the token was authenticated.
  4. Local trust remains for the local-first product; exposing the brain remotely requires the
     brain token even when the global API token is unset.

content.text:
I reviewed everything uncommitted since `e491655`: the earlier agent's work and mine. I found six real defects, one of them a regression I introduced last session, and fixed them all. Each fix has a test that failed before the fix. All four project checks pass, including the full test suite, and every `module.json` is intact. Nothing is committed.

**What I fixed**

| # | Problem | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Tools could get past the sandbox through NeuroCore's own API.** `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` are on the tool network allowlist, and loopback clients need no token, so tool code could call `/settings/save` or `/modules/install` and end up running Python inside the app. A domain that *resolves* to loopback (DNS rebinding, `x.localhost`) also got through. | High | On NeuroCore's own port, tools may call only `/memory/goals` and `/browser_automation/api/`, with `..` and `%` rejected. Other local ports (Ollama, LM Studio) still work. Any other name resolving to loopback is rejected. |
| 2 | **My `.gitignore` change stopped ignoring `modules/skills/data/`.** Writing `data/*` instead of `data/` only matches at the root, so 18 runtime skill files, including a test leftover, appeared as untracked. | Medium | The root `data/` folder is ignored except `.gitkeep`, and nested `data/` folders are ignored again. `data/decoder.key` stays ignored. |
| 3 | **Concurrent chat writes could be lost.** Each worker only reloaded `chat_sessions.json` when its modified-time changed. On filesystems with 1–2 s timestamps, a second worker's new session was silently overwritten. | Medium | Changes are now detected from modified-time, size and file ID together. |
| 4 | **Setting `NEUROCORE_BRAIN_TOKEN` locked out the local brain dashboard.** That contradicts the brain's own design decision (ADR-031). | Medium | Local clients stay trusted; only remote clients need the token. |
| 5 | **The autonomous agent started even when setup failed, and reported success for actions it never ran.** Six action types (`delete_flow`, `use_tool`, `reflect`, `search_knowledge`, `notify_user`, `modify_self_config`) have no implementation. This was audit item A3, which was still open. | Medium (the module is off by default) | `start()` now raises an error after a failed setup. Unimplemented actions return a "not supported" error. |
| 6 | **`NEUROCORE_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` entries with a trailing slash or explicit `:443` never matched,** so allowed origins were quietly rejected. | Low | Both sides are normalized the same way before comparing. |

The README and decision record ADR-035 are updated to match.

**Checked and fine:** atomic writes, backup and recovery in the flow store; the archive extraction size caps; the remote-login and cross-site checks; the agent now running flows through the real flow runner; the ledger locking in the brain module.

**Found but left alone (outside this change set or needs your decision)**
- The built-in default flow has Telegram nodes pointing at a `telegram` module that doesn't exist. They do nothing; replies on that branch are never sent. This was already in `e491655`. Fixing it changes starter data that existing installs already hold.
- Each remote brain-token check runs a slow password hash against every registered user and rewrites a file on success. Correct, but slow; changing the hash scheme needs a data migration.
- Both login checks treat the client names `testclient`/`testserver` (used by the test suite) as local. Exploiting that would need a reverse proxy that passes client headers through unchanged.
- The Docker image build is still untested locally because Docker Desktop isn't running; the new CI job covers it.

It's still all uncommitted. Do you want me to commit it as milestone commits?
So what you do you propose then? Also if you think it is fine as it is to push ; then push.

content.text:
I pushed to `origin/main`, but the new CI didn't actually run. GitHub didn't start any job because your **GitHub account is locked over a billing issue**. That's not a code failure; once billing is sorted, re-running the workflow will test the commit. Until then, the only test evidence is my local runs, and the Docker image build is still untested since Docker Desktop isn't running here.

**What I pushed:** `e491655..3f76ace`, a fast-forward push (no force) of three commits:
- `060870d` **feat(neurocore): add brain runtime; fail closed on auth and sandbox**: the previous agent's brain/meta work plus all the audit and review fixes. The message flags the breaking changes:
  - a non-loopback bind now needs `NEUROCORE_API_TOKEN` or the explicit opt-out;
  - tools only see variables listed in `env_allowlist`;
  - test tools moved to `requirements-dev.txt`.
- `7d95f22` docs(readme): adds the now-tracked `data/` directory to the README file tree.
- `3f76ace` chore(ledger): closes the task.

**Why one big commit:** the brain work and the audit fixes share the README, the decision log, the generated codebase map and the ledger. The decision log's check also requires consecutive record numbers, and my ADR-035 follows the brain's ADR-020–034. Any split would have left a commit that fails the checks on its own. The repo's earlier commits follow the same pattern.

**Checks before pushing:** I checked each commit out into a clean throwaway copy and ran the checks there. On the main commit the full suite passed (1745 passed, 7 skipped), along with the hygiene, docs and secret checks. That run caught one real gap: the README didn't list `data/`, which only became tracked in that commit and so couldn't fail before it. That's why the small `docs(readme)` commit exists.

Running the toolkit's own commit checker from inside NeuroCore checked the outer toolkit repo instead, and failed on a timing overrun in that repo's tests. I then ran the same checks by hand on the NeuroCore commits.

**What I propose next, in order:**
1. **Fix GitHub billing and re-run CI.** This is the first real test on Linux and Windows and of the Docker image.
2. **Decide whether the brain and meta modules should be on by default.** Both ship with `enabled: true`. I only reviewed the brain module's authentication closely, not its full ~10k lines. If you'd rather it stay opt-in like the autonomous agent, that's a one-line change in each `module.json`.
3. **Fix the default flow's Telegram nodes.** They point at a `telegram` module that doesn't exist, so the flow silently never sends replies on that branch. The fix is to switch them to the existing `messaging_bridge` module for new installs.
4. **Your call on F1 (loops in flows):** reject them by default for new and imported flows, keeping a setting so existing saved flows still load.
5. **Remaining hardening, no urgency:**
   - make each remote brain-token check one lookup instead of a slow hash against every registered user;
   - stop treating the client names `testclient`/`testserver` (used by the test suite) as local in the login checks;
   - move `data/memory.sqlite3` and `data/reasoning_book.json` under the configurable state directory. That needs a migration for existing Docker installs.
6. **Longer term:** run untrusted community tools in a container (audit item S6); the Python-level restrictions are defence in depth, not isolation.

Tell me which of 2–4 you want and I'll do them as separate, smaller commits.

- **Commits:** your earlier push approval covered that delivery. I'll treat this as new work and leave it uncommitted until you say otherwise.

    def _compute_execution_order(self):
        """
        Performs a topological sort (Kahn's algorithm) to find the execution order.
        
        This method builds a directed acyclic graph (DAG) from:
        1. Bridge connections (implicit dependencies between bridged nodes)
        2. Regular connections (explicit user-defined edges)
        
        Bridge handling: When a node is bridged, all nodes in its bridge group
        receive the same input. The bridge edges define execution order within
        the group, while connections to any group member feed the entire group.
        
        Cycle handling: If cycles are detected (e.g., A->B->A), we break them
        arbitrarily by picking remaining nodes and forcing them into the order.
        This allows execution to continue even with malformed flows.
        
        Returns:
            list: Topologically sorted list of node IDs for execution
        """
        # Build adjacency list and in-degree count for Kahn's algorithm
        adj = {node_id: [] for node_id in self.nodes}
        in_degree = {node_id: 0 for node_id in self.nodes}

            else:
                # No source specified, use topological order
                execution_queue = deque(self.execution_order)
            
            # Track how many times a node has run to prevent infinite loops
            node_run_counts = {node_id: 0 for node_id in self.nodes}
            max_loops = settings.get("max_node_loops", 1000)
            
            # Parallel set for O(1) membership checks instead of O(n) deque scan
            pending_nodes = set(execution_queue)
            
            while execution_queue:
                node_id = execution_queue.popleft()
                pending_nodes.discard(node_id)
                
                if max_loops > 0 and node_run_counts[node_id] >= max_loops:
                    logger.warning(f"Warning: Node {node_id} hit max execution limit ({max_loops}). Stopping branch.")
                    continue
                
                node_run_counts[node_id] += 1
                
                node_meta = self.nodes[node_id]
                module_id = node_meta['moduleId']
                node_type_id = node_meta['nodeTypeId']

                # 1. Determine Input Data (DAG Logic) - use precomputed incoming_edges for O(1) lookup
                incoming_edges = self.incoming_edges.get(node_id, [])
                
                # Bridge Execution: Process upstream bridge nodes before this node.
                # Independent nodes in the same bridge level run concurrently via
                # asyncio.gather; dependent levels remain sequential.
                # Example: Memory Recall + KB Query (parallel) → System Prompt → LLM Core
                if node_id in self.bridge_groups and node_id not in explicit_start_nodes:
                    bridge_levels = self._get_bridge_levels(node_id)
                    # Start with initial input (excluding the internal routing marker)
                    bridge_input = {k: v for k, v in initial_input.items() if k != "_input_source"} if isinstance(initial_input, dict) else initial_input

                    chain_stopped = False
                    for level in bridge_levels:
                        if chain_stopped:

                        # Skip nodes that are the target itself or already computed
                        to_run = [n for n in level if n != node_id and n not in node_outputs]
                        if not to_run:

"""Brain dashboard route and navigation."""

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from main import app


def test_brain_dashboard_renders():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        response = client.get("/brain/ui")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "AI Brain" in response.text
    assert "Proposals" in response.text
    assert "Reactions" in response.text
    assert "Escape stored" in response.text


def test_brain_dashboard_is_linked_from_navbar():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        response = client.get("/navbar")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert 'href="/brain/ui"' in response.text

"""Which modules a fresh install loads: experimental autonomy stays opt-in."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from main import app

MODULES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "modules"


def _enabled(module_id: str) -> bool:
    with open(MODULES / module_id / "module.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)["enabled"]


def test_experimental_autonomy_modules_ship_disabled():
    assert _enabled("brain") is False
    assert _enabled("autonomous_agent") is False


def test_meta_flow_ships_enabled_because_saved_flows_use_its_nodes():
    assert _enabled("meta") is True


def test_disabled_brain_is_neither_routed_nor_linked():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        dashboard = client.get("/brain/ui")
        navbar = client.get("/navbar")

    assert dashboard.status_code == 404
    assert 'href="/brain/ui"' not in navbar.text

content.thinking: Hashing tokens for a fast index is unsafe here since attacker-controlled tokens would let PBKDF2 be bypassed when guessing weak ones, so I'll instead prefix new tokens with a random, non-secret key ID (`<key_id>.<secret>`) for O(1) lookup plus one PBKDF2 check, keeping legacy tokens unambiguous and throttling `last_used` writes to once per minute. Writing failing-first tests for this next.

def _counting_registry(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    registry = BrainActorRegistry(path=str(tmp_path / "actors.json"), iterations=10000)
    calls = []
    original = registry._hash

    def counted(token, salt):
        calls.append(salt)
        return original(token, salt)

    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_hash", counted)
    return registry, calls


def test_authentication_hashes_once_however_many_actors_exist(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    registry, calls = _counting_registry(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    tokens = [registry.create(f"actor{i}")["token"] for i in range(6)]
    calls.clear()

    actor = registry.authenticate(tokens[-1])

    assert actor.name == "actor5"
    assert len(calls) == 1
    calls.clear()
    assert registry.authenticate(tokens[-1][:-1] + "x") is None
    assert len(calls) == 1


def test_token_key_id_reveals_nothing_about_the_secret(tmp_path):
    registry = BrainActorRegistry(path=str(tmp_path / "actors.json"), iterations=10000)
    token = registry.create("alice")["token"]
    key_id, secret = token.split(".", 1)

    with open(tmp_path / "actors.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        stored = f.read()
    assert key_id in stored
    assert secret not in stored


def test_legacy_and_caller_supplied_tokens_still_authenticate(tmp_path):
    registry = BrainActorRegistry(path=str(tmp_path / "actors.json"), iterations=10000)
    registry.create("chosen", token="my.chosen.token")

    assert registry.authenticate("my.chosen.token").name == "chosen"


def test_last_used_is_written_at_most_once_a_minute(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    registry = BrainActorRegistry(path=str(tmp_path / "actors.json"), iterations=10000)
    token = registry.create("alice")["token"]
    saves = []
    original = registry.save
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "save", lambda data: (saves.append(1), original(data)))

    registry.authenticate(token)
    registry.authenticate(token)

    assert len(saves) == 1
EOF

"""Absolute locations for NeuroCore runtime files.

Runtime state must never depend on the process working directory: starting the app or
its tests from a parent folder must not create settings, databases or caches there.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def project_path(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Return an absolute path inside the NeuroCore project root."""
    return str(PROJECT_ROOT.joinpath(*parts))


def state_path(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Return a path for mutable state, honouring NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR.

    Docker deployments mount one data directory and set NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR, so
    root-level state files do not silently disappear when a container is recreated.
    """
    root = os.environ.get("NEUROCORE_STATE_DIR") or PROJECT_ROOT
    return str(Path(root).expanduser().resolve().joinpath(*parts))

def get_decoder() -> bytes:
    """
    Load or generate the local decoder key (32 random bytes).
    Stored in data/decoder.key as a 64-char hex string.
    This key NEVER leaves the machine and is the basis for all ownership claims.
    If lost, the user permanently loses the ability to manage their marketplace items.
    """
    import secrets, os
    key_file = os.path.join("data", "decoder.key")
    if os.path.exists(key_file):
        try:
            with open(key_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                hex_key = f.read().strip()
            if len(hex_key) == 64:
                return bytes.fromhex(hex_key)
        except Exception as _exc:
            logger.debug("ignored exception: %s", _exc)
    # Generate new random key
    key = secrets.token_bytes(32)
    try:
        os.makedirs("data", exist_ok=True)
        # Write atomically: temp file + rename
        tmp = key_file + ".tmp"
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(key.hex())
        os.replace(tmp, key_file)
    except Exception as _exc:
        logger.debug("ignored exception: %s", _exc)

 "modules/brain/state.py": [],
}
for p in files:
    s=open(p,encoding="utf-8",newline="").read()
    crlf="\r\n" in s; t=s.replace("\r\n","\n"); before=t
    t=re.sub(r'project_path\(\s*"data",\s*', 'data_path(', t)
    t=re.sub(r'state_path\(\s*"data",\s*', 'data_path(', t)
    if p=="core/routers.py":

    n=sum(1 for a,b in zip(before.split("\n"),t.split("\n")) if a!=b)
    # imports
    if "data_path(" in t and not re.search(r'^from core\.paths import .*\bdata_path\b', t, re.M):
        m=re.search(r'^from core\.paths import ([^\n]+)$', t, re.M)
        if m:
            names=[x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",")]
            names.append("data_path")
            # drop names no longer used
            names=[x for x in names if x=="data_path" or re.search(r'\b'+x+r'\(', t[m.end():]) or re.search(r'\b'+x+r'\(', t[:m.start()])]

        else:
            print("NO IMPORT LINE", p)
    open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="").write(t.replace("\n","\r\n") if crlf else t)
    print(p, n)
